import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
customer_segments = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Check if the data is numeric
numeric_cols = customer_segments.select_dtypes(include=['int64', 'float64']).columns

# Plotting the top 5 numeric columns
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.boxplot(data=customer_segments[numeric_cols[:5]], 
            palette=sns.color_palette('Blues', 5), 
            labels=numeric_cols[:5])

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Distribution of Top 5 Numeric Columns')
plt.xlabel('Column Names')
plt.ylabel('Values')

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
plt.xticks(rotation=90)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd

import seaborn as sns

# Check if the data is numeric
numeric_cols = customer_segments.select_dtypes(include=['int64', 'float64']).columns

# Plotting the top 5 numeric columns
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.boxplot(data=customer_segments[numeric_cols[:5]], 
            palette=sns.color_palette('Blues', 5), 
            labels=numeric_cols[:5])

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Distribution of Top 5 Numeric Columns')
plt.xlabel('Column Names')
plt.ylabel('Values')

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
plt.xticks(rotation=90)

# Save the figure
